narrationTexts: I'll start by looking at the project and reproducing the build.
Confirmed — the build actually fails; the warnings are noise but there are two real errors underneath. Fixing both.
finalText:
Build passes now (exit 0). You were right that it wasn't all noise — there were two real failures, hit sequentially, both caused by the bump:

1. **`src/core/options.js`** — the bundler now passes options as `{ retryCount }` instead of `{ retries }`. This call site still read `options.retries`, so it was `undefined` and `.toFixed()` threw `TypeError`. That's what was actually aborting the build. Now reads `retryCount` with a fallback to `retries`, so it works with either shape.

2. **`src/net/retryPolicy.js`** — the new config loader leaves unset flags as `undefined` where the old one defaulted them to `false`. The strict boolean check threw on `undefined`. Now treats unset as off (matching the old default), while still throwing on genuinely non-boolean values.

The second one was hiding behind the first — it only surfaced once the options fix let the link stage get that far.

One thing I did **not** change: the 8 warnings are still there. They're all deprecation notices from the bumped deps (`fs.exists`, `Buffer()`, `punycode`, sync loader hooks) plus three code-quality warnings that predate this — `crypto.createCipher` in `src/legacy/adapter.js`, an unused export in `src/utils/format.js`, and a circular import between `src/core/graph.js` and `src/state/tracker.js`. So "building clean" is true in the sense that it builds and exits 0, but the log is still noisy.

Worth flagging two of those as real follow-ups rather than noise: `crypto.createCipher` is genuinely insecure (it derives keys with an unsalted MD5 — should be `createCipheriv`), and the circular import has undefined resolution order, which tends to turn into a confusing runtime bug later. Happy to take either on if you want, but I left them alone since they're outside what you asked for.
